validity.researcher_notes: Existence/classification confirmed by THREE independent, non-GEM origins, different document classes: (1) Federal Register notice (govinfo.gov, FR-2016-12-30, FR Doc. 2016-31659) publishing FERC's Docket No. CP17-23-000 -- 'Florida Gas Transmission Company, LLC ... filed ... a prior notice request ... requesting authorization to construct, install, own, maintain, and operate its Western Division Project. Specifically, FGT proposes to construct approximately one mile of 36-inch-diameter pipeline loop, relocate an existing receiver, and install one new mainline valve downstream of Compressor Station 11 in Santa Rosa County, Florida. Additionally, FGT proposes to install approximately 100 feet of 8-inch-diameter connection piping ... at a new interconnection ... with Florida Public Utilities Company (FPU) in Escambia County, Alabama, near the Alabama/Florida border ... will provide 68,500 million British thermal units per day ... FGT estimates the cost ... to be approximately $10,655,060.' (2) Natural Gas Intelligence, contemporaneous trade-press ('FGT Expansion to Serve Utility, Chemicals Company', Dec. 29, 2016), independently restates the same one mile of 36-inch loop / 100 feet of 8-inch connection piping / Compressor Station 11, Santa Rosa County, FL / interconnection at the Alabama-Florida border in Escambia County, and cites docket [CP17-23] by name, adding that the 68,500 MMBtu/d splits into 28,500 MMBtu/d FGT firm capacity (potentially 42,000) plus 40,000 MMBtu/d of capacity Ascend Performance Materials agreed to acquire from FPU, phased in with 10,000 MMBtu/d available Oct. 1 (2017) and the rest April 1, 2018. (3) EIA's own 'U.S. Natural Gas Pipeline Projects' workbook (Historical Projects tab) carries an EXACT name match row: Project Name='FGT Western Division Project', Pipeline Operator Name='Florida Gas Trans Co', Project Type='Expansion', Status='Completed', Completed Date=2018-10-25, Year In Service Date=2018, Miles=1, Additional Capacity (MMcf/d)=69, Pipeline Diameter (Inches)='8,36', Cost (millions)=10.7, Pipeline Type='Interstate', Authority='FERC', Docket Number='CP17-23', Crosses State Border='Yes' -- an EXACT match to GEM's current LengthKnown (1.00 mi), Diameter ('8, 36' in) and Capacity (69.00 MMcf/d), and a near-exact match to GEM's SegmentCost (see the separate spec caveat below). Classification confirmed: this is a FERC-jurisdictional interstate transmission mainline-loop expansion (EIA Project Type='Expansion', Pipeline Type='Interstate'), not a gathering/process line -- correctly classified as recorded. DUPLICATE CHECK against the 37-row roster (all pipelines) and specifically the wider 17-row FGT family (P2529/P2594/P2627/P2738/P4029-P4040/P4050/P4060): no other row carries this 1.0mi / '8, 36'in / 69 MMcf/d / CP17-23 signature -- P4040 is the only other 1.0mi FGT row and it is a distinct project (12in diameter, 62 MMcf/d, no CP17-23 match). This is its own distinct, non-duplicated, real, completed, FERC-certificated expansion project -- not a phantom, not a relabel. Opened and read to exhaustion: the Federal Register PDF (full text, both FR Doc. 2016-31659 and its companion 2016-31658, identical CP17-23-000 text), the NGI article (full text), the EIA workbook (Historical Projects tab, full FGT block plus Definitions tab to confirm what State(s)/Beg_State/End_State actually measure), en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Gas_Transmission (full text, corporate-structure context) and kindermorgan.com/Operations/Natural-Gas/Index (full text, corporate-structure context). Of the 9 harvested wiki citations for this shared FGT wiki page: the bit.ly/2smVBv2 link (BANNED -- resolves to abarrelfull.wikidot.com) was never fetched, consistent with the standing ban; eia.gov/maps/layer_info-m.php and eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php are generic navigation pages per the SCOPE brief and were not cited -- used the specific eia-naturalgaspipelineprojects.xlsx workbook instead, which is where the real per-project data lives; fractracker.org's 'National Energy and Petrochemical Map' is a general national map (per its title) and, per an earlier WebFetch of this same wiki page, the generic wiki background text it appears to support ('would add miles to the Alabama and Mississippi section') and a stray 'Length: 93 mi' figure elsewhere on the wiki page do NOT match this specific 1-mile project -- neither was usable and neither is cited (never cite gem.wiki regardless); validity.researcher_notes: The Federal Register notice states FGT 'estimates the cost of the Western Division Project to be approximately $10,655,060'. EIA's Historical Projects workbook independently lists 'Cost (millions)=10.7' for the exact-name-matched 'FGT Western Division Project' row -- these two sources (a FERC regulatory filing figure vs. EIA's own federal statistical database entry) agree with each other to within 0.4%, both landing at ~$10.66-10.7 million. GEM's current SegmentCost value of $11,000,000 is ~3.2% higher than both and appears to be a coarser round-number entry rather than a sourced figure. Flagging rather than silently passing per standing rule 4/SCOPE guidance on SegmentCost; recommend tightening to the sourced figure.
